title: Théorie arithmétique. Théorie de Galois des motifs (1965) : notes manuscites (s.d.), tapuscrit (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context, from the previous page: T_K = R_{K/Q} G_m is the Weil restriction of G_m from K to Q. V_K = Ker(N_K: T_K → G_m) is the norm-one torus. R is the minimal (connected) subtorus of V_K such that V'_K = V_K/R is 'compact', meaning anisotropic over R with compact real points. S^0_K = T_K/R. This gives an exact sequence 1 → V'_K → S^0_K →ε G_m → 1, where ε is induced by the norm. The construction is contravariant in K via the norm maps N_{K'/K}. It is also covariant via the inclusions i_{K,K'}: T_K → T_{K'}, although these are not compatible with ε.

Top of this page: for K ⊂ K' with r = [K':K], diagram (**) records the commutative square ε_{K'} ∘ i_{K/K'} = (λ ↦ λ^r) ∘ ε_K. This holds because N_{K'/Q}(x) = N_{K/Q}(x)^r for x in K.

Corollary 3 (abbreviated 'Cor.'): consider the projective system of the S^0_K, K running over finite extensions of Q inside Q̄. It is canonically isomorphic to (cofinal with) the subsystem indexed by 'Weil' fields, i.e. CM or totally real fields, which may be taken Galois. For such K with K_0 = K ∩ R, one has S^0_K = T_K/V_{K_0}, where V_{K_0} is the norm-one torus of the maximal totally real subfield. The limit is therefore lim T_K/V_{K_0} over CM fields. In modern terms this is the connected Serre group S, the protorus that is the motivic Galois group of CM motives / CM abelian varieties (Serre 1968; Langlands, Deligne, Milne). S^K = T_K/V_{K_0} agrees with Serre's T_K/(Zariski closure of units), since the units of K are of finite index in those of K_0 and are Zariski-dense in the connected norm-one torus of K_0. Reducing an arbitrary number field to its maximal CM (or totally real) subfield is the standard fact that the Serre group of K equals that of its maximal CM subfield, or G_m if there is none.

Corollary 4: there is a unique homomorphism i: G_m → S^0_K with ε∘i(λ) = λ^2. This is the weight cocharacter of the Serre group.
- Uniqueness: Ker ε = V'_K is anisotropic over R, so Hom_Q(G_m, Ker ε) = 0. Two solutions differ by a cocharacter landing in Ker ε.
- Existence: reduce to K a Weil field. If K is real, V'_K is trivial, so ε: S^0_K ≅ G_m and one takes λ ↦ λ^2. If K is CM, K_0 is real, so S^0_{K_0} = G_m; then i = i_{K_0,K} and (**) with r = 2 gives ε∘i = λ^2.

Purpose: this builds the 'Taniyama/Serre' torus as the expected Galois group of the Tannakian category of abelian (CM / Tate-type) motives, including its weight grading, within Grothendieck's Galois theory of motives.
errors: The reduction to Weil fields for existence in Cor. 4 relies on Cor. 3 (or the explicit identification of S^0_K with the Serre group of the maximal CM/real subfield). This is asserted, not proved, on this page.
'Compact' should be read as 'anisotropic over R'. Hom_Q(G_m, ·) = 0 follows because a Q-split subtorus would be R-split. The argument is fine, but implicit.
The normalisation ε∘w = λ^2 (rather than λ^{-2}) is a sign convention. It matches the weight of the Tate/Lefschetz motive up to the usual convention issues.

missed.claim: If the dating (1965-66) is right, Grothendieck independently constructed the connected Serre group, characterised by an archimedean compactness condition rather than by closure of units. He also constructed its weight cocharacter. This predates or is contemporaneous with Serre's 1967-68 McGill lectures and is not credited to him.
missed.quote: on a donc un syst. projectif des T_K/V_{K_0}, où K⊂Q̄ est weilien et K_0=K∩R
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority/independence point for the Serre/Taniyama group as the motivic Galois group of CM motives. It contains no mathematics unknown today.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard: Serre group, CM reduction, weight cocharacter. The interest is historical, as an early independent construction of the Serre group in Grothendieck's motivic Galois theory notes, via a compactness criterion.
transcription_corrections: 'Conj. Main 3' / 'Conj. Main 4' should read 'Cor. Main 3/4', probably 'Corollaire 3' and 'Corollaire 4', continuing 'Corollaire 2' from the previous page. These are corollaries, not conjectures.
'extensions finies de Q̄' should be 'extensions finies de Q (contenues dans Q̄)'.
'weilien' appears to be correct: Grothendieck's term for CM-or-totally-real fields.
